description: HTMLTrust revocation-list cross-origin signer rejection vector 03: a validly-signed document is still rejected because the signer's own origin does not match the origin the list was served from (spec Section 9.8).

key.description: The hostile signer's own key material; the signature below is genuinely valid, which is the point -- a valid signature is not sufficient.

note: The verifier derives the signer's origin from the `signer` value (https://attacker.example) per Section 9.5, and MUST compare it to listServedFromOrigin (https://keys.example) BEFORE resolving the signer at all. They differ, so the document is revocation-unknown regardless of whether its signature verifies -- and it does verify, which is exactly the case this check exists to catch.
